subject: music
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Schubert is especially celebrated for his contribution to which genre?
questions.explain: Schubert composed over 600 Lieder, defining the Romantic art song.

questions.q: In a typical pop or rock song, the section designed to be the most memorable and which usually contains the title and main hook is the...?
questions.explain: The chorus is the most memorable section, typically stating the title and main hook.

questions.q: The studio effect 'reverb' is used to...?
options: Speed up the tempo of a track
Simulate the natural reflections of a sound in a space, adding sense of depth/ambience
Shift the pitch of a vocal up an octave
questions.explain: Reverb recreates the reflections of a physical space, adding depth and ambience to a sound.

questions.q: A tonic pedal is best described as which device?
options: A sustained tonic note held while harmonies change above it
A rapid alternation of tonic and dominant
A modulation to the tonic minor
A melodic ornament on the tonic
questions.explain: A pedal is a sustained or repeated note, the tonic pedal holding the tonic while other parts move through changing harmonies.

questions.q: Brahms is generally regarded as a Romantic composer who upheld which trait?
options: Classical formal structures within a Romantic idiom
questions.explain: Brahms combined Romantic expression with Classical forms such as the symphony and sonata, in the absolute-music tradition.

questions.q: In jazz harmony, 'comping' refers to...?
options: Composing a fully notated arrangement in advance
A pianist or guitarist playing improvised, syncopated chordal accompaniment behind a soloist
Compressing the dynamic range in the mix
Counting the band in before a number
questions.explain: Comping is the improvised, rhythmic chordal accompaniment provided by piano or guitar behind a soloist.

questions.q: The dominant of A minor, when used to create a perfect cadence, normally contains which note as its third?
questions.explain: In the harmonic minor the leading note is raised, so E major (the dominant of A minor) contains G sharp.

questions.q: A diminished seventh chord is built from which stacked intervals?
options: A major third and two minor thirds
questions.explain: The diminished seventh chord consists of three stacked minor thirds, dividing the octave symmetrically.

questions.q: A perfect cadence is formed by which progression?
questions.explain: A perfect (authentic) cadence moves from the dominant (V) to the tonic (I).

questions.q: What characterises a cadential six-four chord?
options: A second-inversion tonic chord on a strong beat resolving to V before the cadence
A dominant chord in third inversion
A tonic chord in root position resolving to V
questions.explain: The cadential 6/4 is a second-inversion tonic chord on an accented beat that delays and decorates the dominant before the cadence.

questions.q: A 4-3 suspension resolves by which means?
options: The fourth steps down to the third
The fourth leaps up to the sixth
The third rises to the fourth
questions.explain: In a 4-3 suspension the dissonant fourth resolves downwards by step onto the consonant third.

questions.q: A recitative in Baroque opera primarily serves which function?
options: To display vocal virtuosity in an aria
To advance the plot through speech-like singing
questions.explain: Recitative uses a free, speech-like vocal style to carry the narrative between arias.

questions.q: Free jazz, associated with Ornette Coleman's album 'Free Jazz' and later John Coltrane, is best described as...?
options: A commercial dance style with simple harmonies
Jazz that abandons fixed chord progressions, metre and predetermined structures in favour of collective spontaneity
Big-band music with written-out arrangements only
A return to strict ragtime forms
questions.explain: Free jazz dispenses with fixed harmony, metre and structure, prioritising collective, spontaneous improvisation.

questions.q: Vivaldi's 'The Four Seasons' is an example of which Baroque genre?
questions.explain: 'The Four Seasons' consists of four solo violin concertos, a leading Baroque solo-concerto example.

questions.q: The 'tabla' is...?
options: A pair of hand drums of different sizes and pitches
questions.explain: The tabla is a pair of tuned hand drums central to North Indian rhythmic accompaniment.

questions.q: The relative minor of G major is which key?
questions.explain: The relative minor shares the key signature of G major (one sharp) and is E minor.

questions.q: 'Fusion' music is best defined as...?
options: A style that blends elements of two or more distinct traditions or genres
Music performed only on acoustic instruments
questions.explain: Fusion combines features of two or more traditions or genres, such as jazz-rock or Indian-Western fusion.

questions.q: A circle-of-fifths progression characteristically moves the bass by which interval?
questions.explain: A circle-of-fifths sequence moves root by root down a fifth (equivalently up a fourth) each step.

questions.q: A 'walking bass' line in jazz is most characterised by which feature?
options: A sustained pedal note held under the harmony
A steady stream of crotchets outlining the chords, usually one note per beat
questions.explain: A walking bass moves in even crotchets, typically one note per beat, threading through the chord tones to drive the harmony forward.

questions.q: The interval from C up to G is which?
questions.explain: C up to G spans seven semitones, a perfect fifth.

questions.q: The Argentine 'tango' is most associated with which instrument providing its characteristic sound?
questions.explain: The bandoneón, a button accordion, gives the tango its distinctive timbre.

questions.q: Which mode results from playing the white notes from D to D?
questions.explain: The Dorian mode runs from D to D on the white notes, with a minor third but a major sixth.

questions.q: Which composer is often called the 'father of the symphony' and the 'father of the string quartet'?
questions.explain: Haydn's extensive output shaped both the Classical symphony and the string quartet.

questions.q: The Indonesian 'gamelan' is primarily an ensemble of...?
questions.explain: A gamelan is built chiefly from tuned metallophones, gongs and drums.

questions.q: In Indian classical music, the 'tala' refers to...?
options: The cyclic rhythmic framework, a repeating cycle of beats
The melodic ornamentation of the soloist
questions.explain: Tala is the rhythmic cycle, a repeating pattern of beats that organises the music in time.

questions.q: The continuous sustained background pitch in Indian classical music, often provided by the tanpura, is called the...?
questions.explain: The drone is the sustained pitch (usually tonic and dominant) supplied by the tanpura beneath the melody.

questions.q: A passing note is which type of non-chord tone?
options: Approached and left by step in the same direction filling a melodic gap
Approached by leap and left by step
A sustained dissonance held over a barline
A note that returns to its starting pitch
questions.explain: A passing note connects two chord tones a third apart, approached and quitted by step in the same direction.

questions.q: Sonata form consists of which three main sections?
questions.explain: Sonata form unfolds in exposition, development and recapitulation, often with an introduction and coda.

questions.q: A Neapolitan sixth chord is a major triad built on which scale degree, usually in first inversion?
questions.explain: The Neapolitan sixth is a major triad on the flattened supertonic (flattened second degree), typically used in first inversion.

questions.q: In music technology, 'sampling' is best described as...?
options: Recording in a single continuous take
Taking a portion of an existing sound recording and reusing it within a new piece
questions.explain: Sampling reuses a fragment of an existing recording as material within a new track.
